chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from a righteous man, peace be upon him, who said:

I asked him about a man who doubts and does not know whether he has prayed one, two, three, or four; his salat becomes confused for him. He said: "All of that?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "Then let him proceed in his salat and seek refuge in Allah from al-Shaytan, for it is likely to go away from him."

This report is to be understood as referring to forgetfulness in supererogatory prayers, and there is nothing in the report stating that he doubted in an obligatory prayer. It is also possible that what is meant is one whose forgetfulness is frequent and who cannot guard against it; in that case it is permissible for him to proceed in his salat, because if repetition were made obligatory for him while forgetfulness is his condition, he would never be free of prayer in any state. As for one whose forgetfulness occurs only occasionally, then it is obligatory for him to repeat the salat according to what we have presented, which indicates what we have mentioned.

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ: al-Shaytan, the source of whispered confusion

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts how many rakʿahs he has prayed in salat?
ai.summary: This report addresses doubt in the number of rakʿahs prayed and instructs the person to continue the salat while seeking refuge in Allah from al-Shaytan. The accompanying discussion explains that this is understood either for supererogatory prayers or for someone afflicted with frequent forgetfulness, while occasional forgetfulness in obligatory prayer requires repetition according to the stated ruling.
